definitions.explanation: The large innermost toe on the foot. In Japanese, toes are usually referred to using the names of the fingers of the hand prefixed with {足|あし}の ('of the foot'), so the big toe is literally 'the thumb of the foot.' Frequently mentioned in medical, sports, and footwear contexts.

examples.japanese: {足|あし}の{親指|おやゆび}が{痛|いた}い。
{靴|くつ}が{小|ちい}さくて、{足|あし}の{親指|おやゆび}が{当|あ}たる。
examples.english: The shoes are small, and they're pressing against my big toe.

examples.japanese: {階段|かいだん}で{足|あし}の{親指|おやゆび}の{爪|つめ}をぶつけてしまった。
examples.english: I bumped the toenail of my big toe on the stairs.

examples.japanese: {足|あし}の{親指|おやゆび}の{付|つ}け{根|ね}が{腫|は}れて、{歩|ある}くのもつらい。
examples.english: The base of my big toe is swollen, and even walking is painful.

notes:
Literally 'the thumb of the foot.' Japanese does not have distinct one-word names for each toe; instead, toes are described by taking the corresponding finger name and prefixing it with {足|あし}の.

TOE NAMES:
- {足|あし}の{親指|おやゆび}: big toe (= thumb of foot)
- {足|あし}の{人差|ひとさ}し{指|ゆび}: second toe (= index finger of foot)
- {足|あし}の{中指|なかゆび}: middle toe
- {足|あし}の{薬指|くすりゆび}: fourth toe (= ring finger of foot)
- {足|あし}の{小指|こゆび}: little toe

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {足|あし}の{親指|おやゆび}をぶつける: to stub one's big toe
- {足|あし}の{親指|おやゆび}の{爪|つめ}: the nail of the big toe
- {足|あし}の{親指|おやゆび}の{付|つ}け{根|ね}: the base of the big toe
- {足|あし}の{親指|おやゆび}が{痛|いた}い: one's big toe hurts
- {足|あし}の{親指|おやゆび}を{骨折|こっせつ}する: to break one's big toe

USAGE:
- In everyday speech, people often just say {親指|おやゆび} when context makes it clear whether the hand or foot is meant — e.g., when pointing to one's foot or discussing shoes.
- The technical medical term is {母趾|ぼし} or {第一趾|だいいっし}, but these are rarely used outside hospitals.
- Common medical conditions named with this word include {巻|ま}き{爪|づめ} ('ingrown toenail') and {外反母趾|がいはんぼし} ('bunion; hallux valgus').
